texts: On day 630 of Year 2, the keepers of the East Row together lit the lanterns of the East Row at sundown.
The lanterns showed mist-light at night.
A crowd of nightmoths gathered at the East Row.
Four sky-cats descended from the cliff-spires.
The four sky-cats hunted the nightmoth crowd at the East Row in summer.
The nightmoth crowd at the East Row shrank.
The surviving nightmoths fled to the Hollows.
The surviving nightmoths reached the Hollows.
The four sky-cats molted during the hunt.
The nightmoths left silken threads on the lanterns of the East Row.

parse: (: cats_hunt_rule (Implication (PartOf $x sk_cats_1) (And (Member (sk_hunt $x) hunt) (Agent (sk_hunt $x) $x) (Theme (sk_hunt $x) sk_crowd_1) (Location (sk_hunt $x) east_row) (Time (sk_hunt $x) summer) (Past (sk_hunt $x)))) (STV 1.0 0.9))

q1_issues.issue: "The nightmoth crowd ... shrank" is an intransitive internal change-of-state, so its subject should be Patient (the class that covers spread / collapse / melt / weaken), not Theme.
"left silken threads on the lanterns" neither creates, destroys, consumes nor physically changes the threads, so the object should be Theme, not Patient.
The per-member distribution rule for that same clause repeats the Patient/Theme role error inside its conclusion.

review.notes: "The keepers of the East Row" is attached with the opaque Possession, but keeper is an agent nominalization whose of-phrase paraphrases as "who keeps the East Row", so the surface-preposition oblique (Of ...) of Complements of nouns and adjectives is arguably the licensed form. The final "The nightmoths" resolves to sk_crowd_1 rather than the earlier sk_moth_1 group -- defensible, but it leaves sk_moth_1 with a single fact.

issues.reason: Thematic roles puts an intransitive subject of an internal change of state (stall, weaken, sag, fade; collapse, melt, spread) in Patient and defines Theme as an object with no change to it, so (Theme sk_shrink_1 sk_crowd_1) mis-types a crowd that does change; the Scalar-change-subject-is-Theme carve-out does not reach it, since no figure is stated and the subject is an entity rather than a value-bearing dimension.

Leaving threads on the lanterns displaces them without creating, destroying, consuming or physically changing them, so the direct-object test of Thematic roles ("does the object itself change?", and when unclear default to Theme) licenses Theme, and (Patient sk_leave_1 sk_thread_1) asserts an alteration the sentence does not state.
The crowd_leave_rule conclusion repeats the same mis-typed role as (Patient (sk_leave $x) sk_thread_1), so every per-member event the rule mints inherits the defect.

new_gaps: Ordinal day-of-year date in a non-Gregorian calendar ("On day 630 of Year 2"): the Time section's structured terms assume (Day n) is a day-of-month sitting under a (Month ...), so a day index of 630 has no licensed slot and is stored indistinguishably from a day-of-month reading. A licensed form would need to carry the calendar system (or an explicit day-of-year term) alongside the year.
adjudication.defect_summary: Issue 0's compliant form is (Patient sk_shrink_1 sk_crowd_1), the intransitive change-of-state subject role. Issue 1's is (Theme sk_leave_1 sk_thread_1), the displaced-not-altered object role. Issue 2's is the same swap inside the rule conclusion, (Theme (sk_leave $x) sk_thread_1); all three have licensed forms, so no gap follows from them.
adjudication.notes: The reviewer's own note on (Possession sk_keeper_1 east_row) is well-founded — Complements of nouns and adjectives bars Possession for an argument and "keeper of the East Row" paraphrases as "one who keeps the East Row", making (Of sk_keeper_1 east_row) the licensed form — but it was filed as a note, not an issue, so it is not adjudicated here. Also unraised: (Location sk_hunt_1 east_row) moves the crowd-modifying "at the East Row" onto the hunting event.
